about: The db-benchmark groupby questions (docs/named-benchmarks.md section 4.3) as commands. {FILE} is the data file's path. 'flags' and 'query' are the argv after the binary: the two forms must give the same bytes and the reference's rows (scripts/bench_named_ref.py --gate). Classes: E expressible; B expressible only up to a bound; X not expressible (a probe argv, the nearest spelling, must be refused with the stated rule, so a feature that lands fails the gate and the entry must be re-classified); D a defect (the command must still fail with a trap status; when it is fixed the gate fails and the entry must be re-classified). No time is recorded here: the later driver (NB2) reads this file.
label: H2O-groupby layout, own generator, seed 108: not the h2oai R generator, so published numbers are not comparable

questions.name: sum v1 by id1
questions.sql: SELECT id1, sum(v1) AS v1 FROM x GROUP BY id1
query: select id1, sum(v1) from '{FILE}' group by id1

questions.name: sum v1 by id1:id2
questions.sql: SELECT id1, id2, sum(v1) AS v1 FROM x GROUP BY id1, id2
query: select id1, id2, sum(v1) from '{FILE}' group by id1, id2

questions.name: sum v1 mean v3 by id3
questions.sql: SELECT id3, sum(v1) AS v1, avg(v3) AS v3 FROM x GROUP BY id3
questions.note: N/K groups: 1e5 at 1e7 rows is the default --max-groups; 1e6 at 1e8 rows is the ceiling. The mean is exact at scale 6, rounded half to even (a choice of the design, docs/named-benchmarks.md 4.3).
query: select id3, sum(v1), mean(v3::dec(6), 6) from '{FILE}' group by id3

questions.name: mean v1:v3 by id4
questions.sql: SELECT id4, avg(v1) AS v1, avg(v2) AS v2, avg(v3) AS v3 FROM x GROUP BY id4
query: select id4, mean(v1, 6), mean(v2, 6), mean(v3::dec(6), 6) from '{FILE}' group by id4

questions.name: sum v1:v3 by id6
questions.sql: SELECT id6, sum(v1) AS v1, sum(v2) AS v2, sum(v3) AS v3 FROM x GROUP BY id6
query: select id6, sum(v1), sum(v2), sum(v3::dec(6)) from '{FILE}' group by id6

questions.name: median v3 sd v3 by id4 id5
questions.sql: SELECT id4, id5, quantile_cont(v3, 0.5) AS median_v3, stddev(v3) AS sd_v3 FROM x GROUP BY id4, id5
questions.blocker: no median and no standard deviation among count, sum, min, max, mean, distinct

questions.name: max v1 - min v2 by id3
questions.sql: SELECT id3, max(v1) - min(v2) AS range_v1_v2 FROM x GROUP BY id3
questions.blocker: the difference of two aggregates is a computed column; max:v1 and min:v2 alone are expressible (the operands)

argv: select id3, max(v1) - min(v2) from '{FILE}' group by id3

questions.name: largest two v3 by id6
questions.sql: SELECT id6, unnest(max(v3, 2)) AS largest2_v3 FROM x WHERE v3 IS NOT NULL GROUP BY id6
questions.blocker: no per-group top-k (--top takes the first groups, not the first values of each group)

questions.name: regression v1 v2 by id2 id4
questions.sql: SELECT id2, id4, pow(corr(v1, v2), 2) AS r2 FROM x GROUP BY id2, id4

questions.name: sum v3 count by id1:id6
questions.sql: SELECT id1, id2, id3, id4, id5, id6, sum(v3) AS v3, count(*) AS count FROM x GROUP BY id1, id2, id3, id4, id5, id6
questions.note: EXPRESSIBLE UP TO A BOUND: the six keys are nearly unique, so there are about N groups, and --max-groups' ceiling is 1,000,000 (limit.too-many-groups above it), so the question fits at 1e6 rows and not at 1e7 or 1e8. A grouping by five or more columns used to trap (exit status 132) at any size (issue 66, fixed: the cache of agg.add_fast overflowed an integer); the six-column command is the same plan as any other grouping.
query: select id1, id2, id3, id4, id5, id6, sum(v3::dec(6)), count(*) from '{FILE}' group by id1, id2, id3, id4, id5, id6
